content.overview: Private nuisance is unlawful interference with a person's use or enjoyment of land. Public nuisance affects the public or a class; a private claimant ordinarily needs special damage beyond the common injury. Remedies include damages and injunction.

sections.heading: Private nuisance
sections.body: Substantial and unreasonable interference — not mere sensitivity. Consider locality, duration, and utility of the defendant's conduct. Who can sue: persons with a proprietary interest in the affected land.

sections.heading: Public nuisance
sections.body: A concept spanning public order and private actions; private action requires special damage. Municipal and environmental statutes often provide parallel remedies.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Plead interest in land, nature of interference, and relief. Evidence: frequency, intensity, impact on ordinary comfort. Consider interim injunction standards.
